questions.text: What is the key distinction between an Architect-of-Record and a Consulting Architect regarding civil liability under Article 1723 of the Civil Code?

options.text: Both assume full civil liability equally.
The Architect-of-Record assumes civil liability for plans and contract documents; the Consulting Architect assumes no liability unless interfering with AoR functions.
The Consulting Architect bears all liability; the AoR has none.
Liability is shared equally between both.

rationale.a: Equal liability across roles ignores the fundamental distinction between primary design authority and specialized consultation.
rationale.c: The Consulting Architect does assume normal liability under service agreements with clients; isolation of all liability is incorrect.
rationale.d: Shared liability contradicts the statutory framework that designates the AoR as primarily responsible.
rationale.correct: The IRR definitions explicitly state the AoR assumes civil liability for plans, specifications, and contract documents signed and sealed, while the Consulting Architect assumes no civil liability unless attempting or succeeding to interfere with or contravene the legal and professional functions of the Architect-of-Record.
rationale.takeaway: This distinction protects specialized consultants from blanket liability while ensuring primary design accountability rests with the AoR; it also creates incentive for consultants to respect the AoR's primary authority.

questions.text: Which law did Republic Act No. 9266 repeal?

options.text: Republic Act No. 8981, which pertains to the Professional Regulation Commission
Republic Act No. 9173, which is related to the nursing profession
Republic Act No. 6571, which is unrelated to architecture

rationale.b: RA 8981 is the PRC Modernization Act; it was not repealed by RA 9266.
rationale.c: RA 9173 is the Health Professions Act; it is unrelated to architecture regulation.
rationale.d: RA 6571 pertains to different professional regulation; it is not the repealed statute.
rationale.correct: RA 9266 explicitly repeals RA 545, the 1950 Architecture Act, after 54 years of governance.
rationale.takeaway: Understand the historical regulatory progression: RA 545 (1950) → RA 9266 (2004) represents the modernization of architecture regulation.

questions.text: How many years of active registered practice in architecture are required for a PRBoA appointment?

rationale.a: Five years is insufficient; the law mandates ten years minimum.
rationale.c: Fifteen years exceeds the statutory threshold; the law says 'at least ten.'
rationale.d: Eight years falls short of the statutory minimum of ten.
rationale.correct: Section 5(c) requires an architect with a valid Certificate of Registration and Professional ID Card and active practitioner status for at least ten (10) years on the appointment date.
rationale.takeaway: The 10-year minimum ensures that Board members possess substantial field experience and understand contemporary practice challenges.

questions.text: What is the composition of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture according to Section 4?

rationale.b: A five-member board was rejected in favor of a more streamlined structure.
rationale.c: No co-chairmen structure exists; singular chair leadership is the model.
rationale.d: Four members would prevent the 1-2-1 staggered year-by-year rotation intended by the law.
rationale.correct: Section 4 explicitly states the Board comprises a chairman and two (2) members appointed by the President.
rationale.takeaway: The three-person composition ensures collegiality without unwieldy committee size; it enables staggered terms that prevent wholesale Board replacement.

questions.text: Describe the relationship between Structural Conceptualization (within architect scope) and Structural Design Documents (within engineer scope) and explain why this boundary exists.

options.text: Architects design all structural elements; engineers only review their work, which can lead to conflicts in design intent and structural integrity

Architects perform structural conceptualization—choosing type, disposition, and arrangement of structural elements—but licensed structural engineers prepare and sign structural design documents; this boundary prevents scope overlap while recognizing the collaborative nature of design.
Engineers perform all structural work; architects contribute nothing, which can result in a lack of architectural coherence in the final design
Both professions interchangeably sign structural documents, which can lead to confusion over responsibility and accountability

rationale.a: If architects designed all, structural engineers would have no role.
rationale.c: Architects contribute significantly to structural conception.
rationale.d: Interchangeable signing violates professional licensing and legal responsibility principles.
rationale.correct: The IRR defines Structural Conceptualization as within architectural scope but reserves structural design document preparation and signing for structural engineers; this respects both professions' domains while enabling collaborative design.
rationale.takeaway: Professional boundaries are permeable at conceptual levels but rigid at final legal responsibility; architects think structurally, engineers engineer structurally and accept legal accountability for structural calculations and specifications.

questions.text: According to the statutory definition, what are the three principles that guide the design and construction of buildings in architecture?

rationale.a: These are modern synonyms but not the statutory terminology.
rationale.c: These terms capture the intent but are not the statute's precise language.
rationale.d: While conceptually related, these are not the three principles named in RA 9266.
rationale.correct: RA 9266's definition states architecture is 'the art, science or profession of planning, designing and constructing buildings in their totality taking into account their environment, in accordance with the principles of utility, strength and beauty.'
rationale.takeaway: These three principles—utility, strength, beauty—echo Vitruvius and form the philosophical foundation of architectural regulation; they reflect the holistic nature of architectural practice.

questions.text: Under Section 6, how many times may a PRBoA member be reappointed after their initial term?

rationale.a: Unlimited reappointments would create indefinite tenure contrary to democratic rotation principles.
rationale.c: Two additional terms would be six years total for Members, exceeding the statutory ceiling.
rationale.d: Reappointment is allowed, but limited to one additional term.
rationale.correct: Section 6 states each member may be reappointed for one full additional term only, limiting maximum tenure to 6 years for Chairman and 4 years for Members.
rationale.takeaway: The single-reappointment limit prevents entrenched power while ensuring sufficient tenure for policy continuity and expertise deployment.

questions.text: Which organization does Section 41 designate as the source from which PRBoA nominees must be drawn?

options.text: IAPOA (Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects, now UAP)
IAPOA (Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects, now UAP)
Philippine Association of Construction Industries, which focuses on construction standards and practices
Association of Professional Engineers, which primarily represents engineering professionals

rationale.b: IAPOA (now UAP) is the correct nominating organization; this option incorrectly identifies an alternative professional body not designated by RA 9266.
rationale.c: PACI represents construction, not the architecture profession.
rationale.d: APE represents engineers, not architects; engineers do not nominate the architecture board.
rationale.correct: Section 41 of RA 9266 designates the IAPOA—now the United Architects of the Philippines, Inc.—as the exclusive source from which PRBoA nominees are submitted to the Commission.
rationale.takeaway: This ensures profession-driven governance; the architectural community itself nominates the regulators, creating accountability and ensuring Board members remain rooted in practitioner concerns.

questions.text: Explain the staggered term system for the three PRBoA members and why it was designed this way.

options.text: All serve 3-year terms for consistency, which simplifies the appointment process but does not ensure continuity

Chairman serves 3 years, Member 1 serves 2 years, Member 2 serves 1 year; this ensures continuity by preventing the President from appointing an entirely new Board simultaneously and guarantees at least one new voice annually.
All serve staggered terms randomly assigned, which could lead to unpredictable board dynamics
Chairman serves 1 year, Members serve 3 years each for member dominance, which is not the intended purpose of the staggered system

rationale.a: Simultaneous terms would allow all-at-once replacement, destabilizing policy.
rationale.c: Random assignment would lack structural intentionality.
rationale.d: Member dominance over chair leadership would invert the hierarchical structure.
rationale.correct: Section 6 prescribes: Chairman 3 years, Member 1 two years, Member 2 one year. This design prevents wholesale Board replacement and ensures institutional memory persists while fresh perspective enters regularly.
rationale.takeaway: Staggered terms are a cornerstone of governance design; they balance continuity against fresh perspective, preventing capture by outgoing administrations or entrenched factions.

questions.text: What is the exact date that Republic Act No. 9266 was signed into law?

rationale.b: December 1, 2004 is the effective date of the IRR, not the statute signature date.
rationale.c: June 1, 2005 is the organizational deadline for the PRBoA, not the statute signature.
rationale.d: This is an incorrect date unrelated to RA 9266's enactment.
rationale.correct: The statute itself states RA 9266 was signed on March 17, 2004, taking effect immediately upon signature.
rationale.takeaway: Know the exact legislative date; it marks the beginning of the modern architecture regulatory era in the Philippines.
